title: Payment API in Express
idea: The payment API exposes payments and refunds as REST resources: the controller validates, the service applies idempotency and money rules, and the repository runs SQL.

analogy.text: A bank counter with numbered tokens. Show the same token twice and the clerk hands back the original receipt instead of serving you again.
analogy.breaks: A reused token with a different request is refused, not answered.

points: `POST /payments` needs an Idempotency-Key; a replay returns 200 with the stored payment.
Only a reused key with a different body gets 422; rule refusals get 409.
The gateway is called between two short writes, never inside a transaction.
Refunds run in one transaction that locks the payment row.

code.title: Layered Express app
code.caption: Repository, service, controllers and error mapping in one file, on a real PostgreSQL. Refund keys work like payment keys and are left out to keep it short.

walk.text: Demo schema: a unique Idempotency-Key, the stored request, and a refund CHECK.
A fake gateway: the token `tok_bad` declines, everything else succeeds.
Repository: SQL only. `settle` changes status only from PROCESSING.
`pay`: replay a known key, refuse a reused key, else insert, charge, settle.
`refund`: lock the row, check state and balance, then add the refund.
Controllers parse with `zod`; Express 5 forwards async throws to the error middleware.
Errors map to status codes; a duplicate key from a race becomes 409.

pitfalls: Never hold a database transaction open while waiting for the gateway.
Store the request with its key; same key, different body must not replay.
Refunds need their own Idempotency-Key; a retried refund must not repeat.

quiz.q: What status does the third POST /payments, reusing k-1, print?
quiz.why: k-1 is stored with a 49900 request. The new body asks for 100, so the stored request differs and the service throws KEY_REUSED: 422.

takeaway: Validate in the controller, dedupe by key, and call gateways outside transactions.

starters: How should the webhook endpoint verify the gateway signature?
What should a client do after a 409 for a concurrent request?
